question: Should this release intentionally invalidate all Codex, Claude, Vertex AI, and pi-session cost caches to guarantee stale scanner offsets are rebuilt?
rationale: The broad cache-version bump is the safest correctness migration, but feature ownership must accept the one-time rescan cost for existing users or request a narrower migration.

options.title: Keep full invalidation
options.body: Accept the one-time rescan across every scanner using the changed JSONL offset semantics after live upgrade proof confirms acceptable behavior.

options.title: Narrow the migration
options.body: Invalidate only cache artifacts whose persisted offsets can exhibit the old incomplete-tail behavior, with focused compatibility tests for unaffected caches.

options.title: Pause for measurements
options.body: Hold the PR until a representative large-history upgrade run quantifies rebuild latency and verifies totals.

recommendation.title: Keep full invalidation
recommendation.body: Accept the one-time rescan across every scanner using the changed JSONL offset semantics after live upgrade proof confirms acceptable behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged scanner hardening work directly covered incremental parsing, cache reuse, refresh paths, and cache-version tests.
